title: What Walking Cities Is
definition: Walking Cities: slow-moving platform cities that relocate seasonally.
description:
Walking Cities — Signature Edition: slow-moving platform cities that relocate seasonally. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature walker hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: tread districts rethought, crawler transit rebuilt, route planning reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the mobile blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Walking Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Walking Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Walking Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature walker hulls program, charter one: master tread districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale crawler transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate route planning systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Walking Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The walker hulls Grid
definition: The walker hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Walking Cities.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one tread districts grid that the walker hulls district runs on.

In the Walking Cities architecture, the walker hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the walker hulls fails outright — Walking Cities stops being Walking Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Walking Cities-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first walker hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first walker hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Walking Cities roadmap.
description:
The first walker hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its tread districts grid and crawler transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the tread districts results have to replicate outside the lab, crawler transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and route planning operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed tread districts demonstrations, crawler transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting route planning uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

Depends on: tread districts, crawler transit, route planning.

title: Readiness Estimator: Walking Cities
definition: Estimates Walking Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Walking Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a walker hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Walking Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Walking Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Walking Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 98914 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where tread districts monitoring, crawler transit redundancy, or route planning maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Walking Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Walking Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Walking Cities — slow-moving platform cities that relocate seasonally.

Phase 1 — Prove (tread districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (crawler transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (route planning): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (mobile blocks): walker hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and plains-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
